correctness.rationale: The coordinate minimum/maximum difference under W obeys |(Wx)_i−(Wx)_j|<=δ(W)R by splitting the zero-mass row difference into signed parts. A direct logistic secant identity σ(u)-σ(v)=sinh[(u-v)/2]/[cosh[(u+v)/2]+cosh[(u-v)/2]] bounds it by tanh(|u-v|/4) under arbitrary shared H. Dini derivatives of active extrema and scalar ODE comparison then prove R<=r with globally invariant cube and Carathéodory uniqueness. Choosing Wδ=[[1+δ,1−δ],[1−δ,1+δ]]/2 and constant H=−β/2 leaves x1+x2=1 invariant; the diameter equation exactly equals r', proving universal sharpness for all q, including q=0. At q=4, d(r^(−2))/dt→2/3 gives r~sqrt(3/(2t)); for q>4 strict concavity of −r+tanh(qr/4) yields unique positive root r*∈(0,1) and two explicit unequal fixed points. Independently checked 1,400 pointwise random-network Dobrushin/secant cases, critical scalar ODE toward sqrt(3/2) and q=6 root≈0.85855963664. Finite trajectories do not prove all times.

Gaubert–Qu contains the underlying Dobrushin diameter operator coefficient and a general nonlinear consensus framework, but its concrete hypotheses do not state the centered logistic tanh envelope and saturation in this dissipative threshold-response flow. These elementary tools are credited, while the exact nonlinear topology-dependent bound and sharp boundary are assessed as surviving. General nonlinear comparison theory may someday imply it with further specialization.
